player_intent: A native development player can host a private test match while the public browser remains dedicated to the 32-player WebRTC tournament and global leaderboard.
acceptance_rule: The native launcher exposes Host Private Match and enters the canonical ENet listen-server path. The restricted browser exposes no private host, room code, manual address, or standalone 2v2 action. Native peer 1 remains authoritative for lobby, shots, damage, and rounds without a Supabase server secret.

nodes.role: Lets only a native build request the canonical ENet private-host path.
Owns the native ENet peer, authoritative lobby, player admission, shots, damage, rounds, and disconnect lifecycle.

must_not_change: SOCOM camera and reticle aim ownership
peer-1 shot, damage, ammunition, and ballistics authority
weapon animation, fire recovery, reload, and hand-contact presentation
browser WebRTC tournament and leaderboard front door
visual_check: Open a native build and confirm Host Private Match still creates an ENet lobby and invite. Open the restricted browser build and confirm that action, room-code entry, and manual join controls do not exist.

system_delta.reason: Replace browser-hosted private match presentation with automatic public WebRTC tournament matchmaking. Retain the existing native ENet private host only as a bounded development tool.

candidate.system: Native-only ENet private host separated from the automatic browser WebRTC tournament
